skill.name: relight
skill.description: Relight still images with RunComfy using Qwen Edit Relight and fallback edit models for color temperature, direction, intensity, and mood changes.
skill.summary: Relight still images through RunComfy with model routing and lighting prompt guidance.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are false positives from Markdown backticks, model identifiers, and documentation links. Confirmed risks are the scoped RunComfy CLI command surface, external processing of user images and prompts, and local token storage in a hidden config path.

remediation.suggestion: Add an explicit consent note before sending private images or prompts to RunComfy services, and document retention expectations.

remediation.issue: API token persistence in a hidden config file
remediation.suggestion: Document token revocation, least-privilege token use, and safer CI usage with RUNCOMFY_TOKEN instead of persistent login on shared machines.

remediation.issue: CLI installation through npm or npx
remediation.suggestion: Keep installation guidance in the dedicated CLI skill, recommend pinned versions, and avoid automated installs without user confirmation.

content.value_statement: Still images often need new lighting without another shoot. This skill routes relight requests to RunComfy models with practical prompt guidance.
actual_capabilities: Routes still-image relighting requests to Qwen Edit 2509 Relight LoRA.
Suggests fallback edit models for broader image edits with lighting changes.
Shows RunComfy CLI invocation patterns for image inputs and output folders.
Guides prompts for light source, color temperature, direction, and intensity.
Covers product, portrait, landscape, reference-match, and batch relighting patterns.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, and an available API token.
Processes still images only; video relighting is outside this skill.
Sends image references and prompts to external RunComfy services.
Output quality depends on clear preservation instructions and model availability.

use_cases.title: Refresh Product Photos
use_cases.description: Apply consistent studio or lifestyle lighting to catalog images without reshooting each product.

use_cases.title: Adjust Portrait Mood
use_cases.description: Change a portrait from flat light to golden hour, rim light, or soft window light.

use_cases.title: Prototype Lighting Directions
use_cases.description: Compare lighting directions, color temperatures, and contrast levels before production editing.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Relight
prompt_templates.prompt: Relight this image with soft warm window light from the left. Preserve the subject, pose, framing, and colors.

prompt_templates.title: Product Lighting Pass
prompt_templates.prompt: Relight this product image as a clean studio setup with a warm key light, soft fill, and natural shadow.

prompt_templates.title: Reference Lighting Match
prompt_templates.scenario: Source image should match another lighting style.
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the lighting direction, temperature, and contrast from the reference image while preserving the original subject identity.

prompt_templates.title: Batch Brand Relight
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for a set of related images.
prompt_templates.prompt: Relight this image set with the same late-afternoon brand lighting, consistent shadow direction, and preserved product colors.

output_examples.input: A product photo needs warm window light and a softer shadow.
output_examples.output: The skill selects Qwen Edit Relight and returns guidance for a warm left-side key light with preserved product color.

output_examples.input: A portrait should look like golden hour while keeping the person recognizable.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a relight prompt with warm rim light, soft front fill, and explicit identity preservation.

output_examples.input: A landscape needs a blue hour mood change and broader scene handling.
output_examples.output: The skill routes to a description-based edit model and frames the lighting change as a full-scene adjustment.

best_practices: Describe light source, direction, color temperature, and intensity in the same request.
State what must be preserved, including subject identity, framing, pose, and product color.
Use only image URLs or files that the user explicitly approved for external processing.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for text-to-image generation from scratch.
Do not submit private images without confirming external processing is acceptable.
Do not combine many unrelated edits when the goal is precise relighting.

faq.question: Does this skill create new images from text only?
faq.answer: No. It relights existing still images and points text-to-image requests to a different workflow.

faq.question: Which model does it use by default?
faq.answer: It uses Qwen Edit 2509 Relight LoRA when the request is focused on lighting changes.

faq.question: Can it match lighting from a reference image?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends a reference-based edit route when a target lighting image is available.

faq.question: Does it support video relighting?
faq.answer: No. The documented CLI route is for still images only.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: Users need the RunComfy CLI, authentication, and access to the selected RunComfy model endpoint.

faq.question: Will prompts and images leave my machine?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill uses RunComfy services, so image references and prompts are processed externally.
